about:
# Krool World Forever

Small quality-of-life features for **World of Warcraft: Forever**, in one addon. Each feature has its
own on/off switch, so you keep what you want and turn off the rest.

**[Download the latest release](https://github.com/Krool/KroolWorldForever/releases/latest)**, or get it on
[CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/krool-world-ui).

`/kw` (or the addon button on the minimap) opens the **Krool World hub**: one card per feature with
what it is doing right now, its on/off switch, and the way in (its window or its settings).

| Feature | What you get | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Quest Trash** | A keep or delete verdict on quest item tooltips. `/fqt` opens a window that sorts your bags (and bank) into Can Delete, Keep and Still Checking. | QuestieDB |
| **Kill Value** | Expected gold per kill on creature tooltips: coins plus each drop's chance times its price, plus the skinning if you can skin it. Learns real drop rates from what you loot. Herbs, mining veins and fishing pools show their value too. | Nothing (Auctionator optional) |
| **Setups** | Save a character's action bars, keybindings, macros, Edit Mode layout, interface settings, chat text size, addon list and this addon's settings, then apply them to another character. A window shows which setup goes onto which character, and a check, warning or X per part afterwards. New characters can start from a saved setup. | Nothing |
| **Rare Alert** | A sound, a screen message and a chat line when a rare enemy is near, with what it is worth and its best drops, plus a marker button and a key that target it and mark it (a skull by default). One alert per spawn. The button goes once the rare has your marker or dies; right-click hides it, shift-right-click ignores that rare (the Stormwind canal crocolisk is ignored out of the box). Rares are noticed through enemy nameplates, which Forever starts with off: the hub's Plates On button turns them on. | Nothing |
| **Disenchant Value** | On weapon and armor tooltips (green and up): what the item disenchants into, and what that is worth at auction. Hold Shift for each material's chance and price. If Auctionator shows a Disenchant line of its own, this one steps aside. | Auctionator (for prices) |
| **Camp Guide** | Hover a campfire or a camp object (the chair, the lodestone and the rest) for the buff it gives at your level, and whether a class buff you already have covers it (the Lodestone does not stack with Blessing of Might). The campfire says how its buffs work and lists the objects you have hovered around it. The Camp Benefits buff names any bonus in it that one of your class buffs overlaps. | Nothing |
| **Skill-Up Odds** | In the crafting window: the chance each recipe gives a skill point, beside its arrow. It is the common straight line from 100% at yellow to 0% at grey, tuned by every yellow or green craft on your characters (hover for the numbers and what a point costs). A Next Skill Point panel ranks your learned recipes by the gold a point costs on average, and only reorders when a recipe is clearly cheaper. | Nothing (Auctionator optional) |
| **Sayge's Fortune** | When Sayge at the Darkmoon Faire can give you your next fortune. His wait is 4 hours from your last fortune, counted only while that character is logged in, and dying does not end it, but the game hides it: this counts it on every character and shows what is left on the hub, on Sayge's tooltip and on the fortune buff. If you die with the buff, a chat line says when you can get the next one. | Nothing |
| **Least Valuable** | A copper coin on the corner of the bag slot worth the least, so you know what to sell or drop first: its whole stack at the best of its vendor price, auction price and disenchant value. It never marks quest items, keys, ammunition, class reagents, profession tools, unopened containers (clams, lockboxes), equipment-set gear, worthless items like the Hearthstone, or an unscanned green. The coin shows in the default bags. `/kwl ignore` skips anything else you keep. When your bags are full and you try to loot, a card beside the loot window names that item and its value against the loot's, says whether the loot is worth making room for, and lets you browse the next cheapest or never mark one. The card keeps off your open bags. Its Delete button deletes the item it shows when you click it, after asking (both can be switched off); nothing is deleted by itself. | Nothing (Auctionator optional) |
| **Quest Reward Value** | A coin on the quest reward worth the most, at the quest giver and in the quest log, at the best of its vendor price, auction price and, for an enchanter, its disenchant value, and that value on each reward's tooltip. A reward that binds when picked up has no auction price. It never picks the reward for you. | Nothing (Auctionator optional) |
| **One-Button Fishing** | One key casts your line and, while it is out, reels in the bite. Set it under Key Bindings > AddOns > Krool World. With a fishing pole in your main hand, a double right-click does the same. Every cast and reel is your own key press or click. | Nothing |
| **Reagent Uses** | Hold Ctrl (or the key you choose) over a crafting material and its tooltip lists every recipe that uses it, grouped by profession, yours first. Each recipe is colored by your skill, with how many of the material it takes, how many more recipes use what it makes, and who knows it (you, and each other character once it has opened its profession window) or where it is learned (Trainer 175, Vendor, Drop...). Built from Forever's own recipe data, including the recipes Forever added. | Nothing |
| **Market Movers** | After Auctionator scans the auction house, a window beside it shows what is priced unusually, in four tabs: materials and other items that rose or fell against their usual price (the middle price of up to a week), bargains listed under the vendor price or far under usual, and how the items in your bags stand. Each row has a small trend line. Click a row to search the item in Auctionator. Gear is left out. It keeps its own daily record of the scans, so the first comparison comes the day after your first scan. It never buys, bids, posts or cancels. `/kwm` | Auctionator |
| **Boats And Zeppelins** | A pin on the world map at every boat dock and zeppelin tower. Hover it for where the boat or zeppelin goes. The routes come from Forever's own data, so the new ones (Stormwind to Darkshore) are there with the classic ones. Zone maps show their docks; continent maps and the world map can too. Two that leave from one place share a pin. High Order Skyborne also get a pin at Dalaran's portal to Stormwind, on zone maps. It shows every route in the game's data: it cannot tell when the next boat arrives, or whether a route is running yet. `/kwb` | Nothing |

All fourteen are on by default.

**Your characters.** Reagent Uses, Sayge's Fortune and Setups list your other characters. Every
character is included by default. To leave out bank or mule alts, untick them in `/kw chars` (or
use the hub's Stop Tracking This Character button while on one). Nothing is deleted: tick a
character again and it is back.

**Only want one or two?** Every feature also comes as its own addon, named "KW" plus the feature
(KW Quest Trash, KW Kill Value, ...). They are attached to each
[release](https://github.com/Krool/KroolWorldForever/releases/latest) and listed on CurseForge.
Install either the bundle or the single ones: next to the bundle, a single one switches itself
off and says so.

## How it behaves

- **Advice only.** Quest Trash, Kill Value, Rare Alert, Disenchant Value, Camp Guide, Skill-Up Odds, Sayge's Fortune, Least Valuable, Quest Reward Value, Reagent Uses, Market Movers and Boats And Zeppelins never delete, sell, buy,
  loot, craft or click anything for you. Rare Alert's marker comes from your own click or key press: the game does not let an
  addon place one by itself. One-Button Fishing works the same way: it only points your key at the
  cast or the bobber, out of combat, and puts back the interact settings it borrows when the line is in. Least Valuable has the one
  Delete button, on its Bags Full card: it deletes the one item the card shows, only when you click it, and asks first unless you
  switch the question off. Nothing is ever deleted by a timer, a scan or a setting. Setups is the one feature that changes your UI: only out of combat,
  only when you click Apply (or for a brand-new level 1 character, if you marked a setup for that),
  and always with an undo snapshot first. A character with any experience is never changed without
  a click.
- **Plays by Forever's addon rules.** Nothing reads combat data Blizzard hides from addons. Every
  feature checks for hidden ("secret") values and steps aside instead of erroring. Inside instances,
  where creature tooltip data is hidden, Kill Value shows nothing.
- **Errors stay out of your way.** Tooltip and event code runs protected, so a bad value skips a line
  instead of throwing a Lua error.

## Install

1. Download `KroolWorldForever-<version>.zip` from the
   [releases page](https://github.com/Krool/KroolWorldForever/releases/latest).
2. Unzip it into your Forever AddOns folder, so you end up with
   `World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\KroolWorldForever\KroolWorldForever_Forever.toc`.
3. Restart the game (or `/reload`) and check that **Krool World Forever** is enabled in the AddOns list
   on the character screen.

Optional companions:

- **QuestieDB** (the CurseForge app installs it with Questie; by hand it is its own download): required for Quest Trash. Without it Quest Trash says so at login
  and the other features work normally.
- **Auctionator**: auction house prices for Kill Value, Disenchant Value, Skill-Up Odds and Least
  Valuable. Without it Kill Value uses vendor prices, Disenchant Value names the materials without
  prices, Skill-Up Odds prices only the reagents it has seen at a vendor, and Least Valuable goes by
  vendor prices and leaves greens unmarked. All four mark auction prices more than 3 days old, and
  Kill Value, Skill-Up Odds and Least Valuable pick up new prices as soon as an Auctionator scan
  finishes. Market Movers needs it: its report is built from Auctionator's full scans.

## Slash commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/kw` | Open the hub (again to close it) |
| `/kw settings` | Open the settings |
| `/kw list` | List the features and whether each is on |
| `/kw errors` | List the errors the addon caught (`/kw errors clear` empties the list) |
| `/kw <feature>` | Open that feature's window, or its settings (`questtrash`, `killvalue`, `setups`, `rares`, `disenchant`, `camp`, `skillup`, `fortune`, `leastvaluable`, `rewardvalue`, `fishing`, `reagents`, `movers`, `transports`) |
| `/kw <feature> on` / `off` | Turn one feature on or off |
| `/kw chars` | Your characters, with a Track box each (untracked ones are left out of every character list) |
| `/kw untrack [name]` / `track [name]` | Leave a character out of the lists, or bring it back (no name: the one you are on) |
| `/kw forget <name>` | Drop a character from the list and from Reagent Uses and Sayge's Fortune (saved setups are kept) |
| `/fqt` | Open the Quest Trash window: your bags (and the bank while it is open), deletables first |
| `/fqt print` / `status` | The same list in chat; whether the quest data is ready |
| `/fkv` | Full value breakdown for your target |
| `/fkv id <npcId>` | Breakdown for any creature by id |
| `/fkv status` / `config` / `help` | Data sources, current settings, all commands |
| `/fkv reset learned` | Erase the drop rates learned from your loot |
| `/kws` | Open the Setups window |
| `/kws save [name]` | Save this character as a setup |
| `/kws list` | List saved setups |
| `/kws undo` | Undo the last apply on this character |
| `/kwr ignore` | Ignore your target (or the last rare seen) |
| `/kwr unignore <name or id>` / `list` | Stop ignoring one; show the ignore list |
| `/kwr test` | Show the mark button with a test entry, to place it (shift-drag) and try your key |
| `/kwr nameplates` | Turn enemy nameplates on (rares are noticed as soon as their nameplate shows) |
| `/kwd` | Disenchanting material prices from Auctionator (which ones still have none) |
| `/kwd seen` | Your disenchants, checked against the tables (what came out, and anything they do not list) |
| `/kwc` | Every camp buff at your level, which ones a class buff of yours covers, and your Camp Benefits time |
| `/kwu` | How your crafts sit against the line, overall and range by range |
| `/kwu status` / `panel` | Where the numbers come from (data build, crafts logged); show or hide the Next Skill Point panel |
| `/sayge` | When Sayge gives your next fortune, on this character and your others this faire |
| `/kwl` | The five least valuable bag slots, and what was not counted (quest items, tools...) |
| `/kwl ignore` / `ignore <item>` | Never mark the marked item, or any item (shift-click it into the chat line) |
| `/kwl unignore <item>` / `ignored` | Mark it again (item, id or name); show the ignore list |
| `/kwfish` | Your fishing key, and whether a pole is equipped for double right-click |
| `/ru` | Reagent Uses' settings (`/ru chars` opens the character list) |
| `/kwb` | The boats and zeppelins of the zone you are in (`/kwb all` lists every dock) |
| `/kwm` | Open the Market Movers window (`/kwm bargains` and `/kwm bags` open those tabs, `/kwm print` puts the top moves in chat, `/kwm reset` puts the window back beside the auction house) |

The mark key and the fishing key are under **Key Bindings > AddOns > Krool World** (in a KW addon, under its own name). `/kwf` and `/kroolworld` work like
`/kw`; `/questtrash`, `/killvalue`, `/kwsetups`, `/rarealert`, `/disenchantvalue`, `/campguide`,
`/skillup`, `/kwsayge`, `/leastvaluable`, `/reagentuses`, `/marketmovers` and `/kwboats` are long forms of `/fqt`, `/fkv`, `/kws`,
`/kwr`, `/kwd`, `/kwc`, `/kwu`, `/sayge`, `/kwl`, `/ru`, `/kwm` and `/kwb`.

A single KW addon answers its own command (for example `/fqt` in KW Quest Trash), and also takes
`settings`, `errors`, `chars`, `track`, `untrack` and `forget` after it (`/fqt settings`).

## Settings

Every feature has a page under **Options > AddOns > Krool World Forever** with an Enabled switch and
its own settings. The tables below are generated from the features' own definitions by
`tools/settings-doc.js`. Do not edit them by hand.

### Quest Trash

Marks quest items you can safely delete on their tooltips. Needs QuestieDB.

On by default: yes. Toggle: `/kwf questtrash on|off`. Commands: `/fqt, /questtrash`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Show Verdict On Tooltips | On | Adds a keep or delete line to quest item tooltips. |
| List The Quests Involved | On | Shows up to four quests and their status under the verdict. |

### Kill Value

Adds the expected gold per kill to creature tooltips: coins plus drop table times vendor or Auctionator prices. Herbs, mining veins and fishing pools show what they yield the same way.

On by default: yes. Toggle: `/kwf killvalue on|off`. Commands: `/fkv, /killvalue`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Learn From My Loot | On | Records what corpses drop so new or rebalanced creatures get real numbers. |
| Use Vendor Prices | On | Vendor sell price as fallback and floor. |
| Use Auctionator Prices | On | If Auctionator is installed, price drops from the auction house minus the cut. |
| Add My Skinning To The Total | On | When you know Skinning (or Herbalism or Mining, for creatures gathered that way) with enough skill for the creature, its skinning value is part of the total. |
| Show Skinning Value | Off | Also shows the skinning value of creatures you cannot skin (not part of the total). |
| Show On Friendly Creatures | Off | Also adds the line to creatures you cannot attack. |
| Show On Herbs, Veins And Pools | On | Adds the expected value of a herb, mining vein or fishing pool to its tooltip: everything it yields at vendor or Auctionator prices. A vein counts all its mines (2 to 4), a pool all its catches. Says so when your Herbalism or Mining is too low. |
| Login Message | On | Prints one line at login. |
| Contributor Lines | 3 (0 to 10) | Top drops listed under the total (0 = none). |
| Auction House Cut % | 5 (0 to 100) | Taken off Auctionator prices. |

### Setups

Save a character's action bars, keybindings, macros, Edit Mode layout, interface settings, chat text size, addon list and Krool World settings, and apply them to another character. /kws opens the window.

On by default: yes. Toggle: `/kwf setups on|off`. Commands: `/kws, /kwsetups`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Offer A Setup On New Characters | On | The first time a character logs in with this addon, open the Setups window so you can start from a saved setup. Preselects the setup marked for new characters. |
| Apply The Default Setup Automatically | On | When a setup is marked Use For New Characters, a brand-new character (level 1, first login) gets it a few seconds after logging in, and the Setups window shows what changed. Characters that are not brand-new get the picker instead. Off: the picker opens instead. |
| Reload Automatically After Apply | On | Edit Mode layouts and the addon list take effect after a UI reload. On: Apply reloads by itself when needed. Off, and after the automatic apply on a new character (the game allows a reload only from a click): a Reload Now button appears. |
| Auto Snapshot Each Character | On | Keep one automatic setup per character, refreshed after login and shortly after you change bars, keybindings, macros, Edit Mode or settings, so any character can copy any other. |
| Applied Keybindings Are Per Character | On | On: applying a setup saves its keybindings for this character only. Off: for the whole account, which changes every character that uses account keybindings. |
| Clear Bar Slots The Setup Leaves Empty | On | On: an apply makes your bars match the setup exactly. Off: only fills slots, keeping anything already in a slot the setup leaves empty. |

### Rare Alert

Tells you when a rare enemy is near and gives you a button and a key that target it and put a raid marker on it. The game lets only a click or key press set a marker, so it never marks by itself.

On by default: yes. Toggle: `/kwf rares on|off`. Commands: `/kwr, /rarealert`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Play A Sound | On | The raid warning sound when a rare shows up. |
| Show A Screen Message | On | The rare's name in the middle of the screen, like a raid warning. |
| Chat Message | On | A chat line with the rare's name and level, and how to target it. A second line says what it is worth and its best drops. |
| Show The Mark Button | On | A marker button near the top of the screen while a rare is near. Click it to target the rare and mark it. It goes once the rare has your marker or dies, or a minute after you last saw it. Right-click hides it; shift-right-click ignores that rare; shift-drag moves it. The key in Key Bindings > AddOns > Krool World works either way. |
| Raid Marker | 8 (1 to 8) | Which marker the button puts on the rare: 8 skull, 7 cross, 6 square, 5 moon, 4 triangle, 3 diamond, 2 circle, 1 star. |

### Disenchant Value

On weapon and armor tooltips: what the item disenchants into, and what that is worth at Auctionator's prices.

On by default: yes. Toggle: `/kwf disenchant on|off`. Commands: `/kwd, /disenchantvalue`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Show On Item Tooltips | On | Adds the disenchant value to weapon and armor tooltips (green, blue and purple). |
| Always List The Materials | Off | Lists each material with its chance and price. Off: hold Shift over the item to see them. |
| Hide When Auctionator Shows Its Own | On | Auctionator can add a Disenchant line of its own (its Tooltips settings). When it is on the tooltip, this addon adds nothing. Off: both show. |

### Camp Guide

Hover a campfire or a camp object (the chair, the lodestone and the rest) for the buff it gives at your level, and whether a class buff you already have covers it. The campfire lists the objects you have hovered around it.

On by default: yes. Toggle: `/kwf camp on|off`. Commands: `/kwc, /campguide`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Show On Camp Objects | On | Adds each camp object's buff at your level to its tooltip, and on the campfire how its buffs work and the objects you have hovered there. Only while the game says a campfire is nearby. |
| Notes On Camp Benefits | On | On the Camp Benefits buff, names any camp bonus in it that does not stack with a class buff you have, such as the Lodestone with Blessing of Might. |

### Skill-Up Odds

In the crafting window: the chance each recipe gives a skill point, and a Next Skill Point panel that ranks your recipes by the gold a point costs. Blizzard never published the chance, so it is the common straight line from 100% at yellow to 0% at grey, tuned by every yellow or green craft on your characters.

On by default: yes. Toggle: `/kwf skillup on|off`. Commands: `/kwu, /skillup`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Show Odds In The Recipe List | On | Puts the skill-up chance beside each recipe's arrow. Hover it for how it is worked out and what a point costs. |
| Show The Next Skill Point Panel | On | Docks a panel beside the crafting window that ranks your learned recipes by the gold a skill point costs on average. |
| Subtract What The Result Sells For | On | Takes the crafted item's vendor price off the cost of a craft. |
| Value The Result At Auction | Off | Uses the crafted item's Auctionator price (after the 5% cut) when it beats the vendor price and is at most 3 days old. Only if you will really sell it there. |
| Measure Your Crafts | On | Records each craft's skill before and after, account-wide. Your yellow and green crafts tune the odds. |

### Sayge's Fortune

When Sayge at the Darkmoon Faire can give you your next fortune. His wait is 4 hours from your last fortune, counted only while that character is logged in, and dying does not end it, though the fortune itself is lost. The game hides that wait, so this counts it, on every character.

On by default: yes. Toggle: `/kwf fortune on|off`. Commands: `/sayge, /kwsayge`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Show On Sayge And Your Fortune | On | Adds when you can get your next fortune to Sayge's tooltip and to the fortune buff's tooltip. |
| Tell Me If I Lose It | On | When your fortune goes early (you died), says in chat when Sayge gives the next one. |
| Tell Me When The Wait Is Over | On | Says in chat when Sayge's 4-hour wait ends while you are logged in. |

### Least Valuable

Marks the bag slot worth the least, so you know what to sell or drop first: its whole stack at the best of its vendor price, auction price and disenchant value. It never marks quest items, keys, ammunition, class reagents, profession tools, unopened containers, equipment-set gear, items worth nothing (the Hearthstone), or anything you /kwl ignore.

On by default: yes. Toggle: `/kwf leastvaluable on|off`. Commands: `/kwl, /leastvaluable`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Mark It In Your Bags | On | A copper coin in the top-right corner of the slot worth the least, in the default bags. Its value counts the whole stack. /kwl ignore  stops an item from being marked. |
| Say It On The Tooltip | On | Adds what the marked slot is worth, and at which price, to its tooltip. |
| Bags Full Card | On | When a full bag stops a pickup, shows a small card with your least valuable item and what the loot is worth, so you can decide what to make room for. It keeps off your open bags, and it never drops, sells, loots or deletes anything by itself. |
| Delete Button On The Card | On | Adds a Delete button to the Bags Full card. It deletes the item the card shows, to make room, and only when you click it. A deleted item cannot be brought back. Off: the card only shows text and a mark. |
| Confirm Before Deleting | On | The card's Delete button asks before it deletes. Off: one click deletes. A rare or better item always asks. |

### Quest Reward Value

Marks the quest reward choice worth the most, with a coin on its button, at the quest giver and in the quest log: each choice at the best of its vendor price, Auction House price (Auctionator) and disenchant value. It only marks; you still pick the reward. Without Auctionator it counts vendor prices only.

On by default: yes. Toggle: `/kwf rewardvalue on|off`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Mark Best Reward | On | A copper coin on the reward choice worth the most, counting the whole stack at its best price (vendor, Auction House or disenchant). Nothing is marked when choices tie or are worth nothing. |
| Value On Reward Tooltips | On | Adds what a reward choice is worth, and at which price, to its tooltip, at the quest giver and in the quest log. |

### One-Button Fishing

One key casts your line and reels in the bite: set it in Key Bindings > AddOns > Krool World. With a fishing pole in your main hand a double right-click does the same. Every cast and reel is your own key press or click; the addon only re-points keys, and only out of combat.

On by default: yes. Toggle: `/kwf fishing on|off`. Commands: `/kwfish`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Double Right-Click To Fish | On | While a fishing pole is in your main hand, a quick double right-click casts, and reels in when the line is out. Not while moving, mounted, swimming, stealthed, in a vehicle or in combat. |

### Reagent Uses

Hold a key over a crafting material and its tooltip lists every recipe that uses it, grouped by profession and colored by your skill, with who knows each one or where it is learned.

On by default: yes. Toggle: `/kwf reagents on|off`. Commands: `/ru, /reagentuses`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Show With | Ctrl (one of Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Always Show) | The key to hold over a crafting material to list the recipes that use it. Always Show lists them on every material's tooltip. |
| Show Hint | On | While the key is up, one line on the tooltip says how many recipes use the material. |
| Show Other Characters | On | Names your other tracked characters who know each recipe. A character is remembered after it opens its own profession window with this on. |
| Hide Grey Recipes | Off | Leaves out recipes that can no longer give you a skill point. |
| Recipes Shown | 15 (5 to 50) | How many recipes the tooltip lists. Past that, each profession only shows its count. |

### Market Movers

After Auctionator scans the auction house, shows what is priced unusually: trade materials and other items that rose or fell against their usual price, bargains listed under the vendor price or far under usual, and how the items in your bags stand. Gear is left out. It keeps its own daily record of the scans, so the first comparison comes the day after your first scan. Needs Auctionator.

On by default: yes. Toggle: `/kwf movers on|off`. Commands: `/kwm, /marketmovers`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Open After A Full Scan | On | Opens the window beside the auction house when Auctionator finishes its first full scan of each visit, if anything moved or there is a bargain. It closes with the auction house. Later scans in the same visit only update it. |
| Button On The Auction House | On | A small button above the auction house's top right corner with the number of movers and bargains. A click opens or closes the window. |
| Common At | 40 (10 to 200) | A trade material listed in at least this many units, now or usually, goes under Materials. Fewer, and it goes under Other. |
| Ignore Under (Listed) | 10 (1 to 50) | Other items listed in fewer units than this, now and usually, are left out: one odd listing of a rare item is not a market move. |
| Smallest Change (%) | 10 (5 to 50) | Price moves smaller than this are left out. |
| Bargain At (% Under Usual) | 30 (10 to 80) | An item this far under its usual price, that usually has stock, is listed under Bargains. |
| Ignore Under (Silver) | 1 (0 to 100) | Items cheaper than this both now and usually are left out: a few copper either way is not news. |
| Rows Per List | 8 (4 to 25) | How many items each list shows, biggest moves first. |

### Boats And Zeppelins

Puts a pin on the world map at every boat dock and zeppelin tower. Hover a pin for where it goes. The routes come from the game's own data, so the new ones are there too. It cannot tell when the next one arrives. High Order Skyborne also get a pin at Dalaran's portal to Stormwind, on zone maps.

On by default: yes. Toggle: `/kwf transports on|off`. Commands: `/kwb, /kwboats`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Show On Continent Maps | On | Also shows the pins on the continent maps and the world map. Off: zone maps only. |
| Pin Size | 22 (12 to 36) | How big a pin is on the map. |

## FAQ

**Which game is this for?** World of Warcraft: Forever only (`_forever_` install folder, Interface
16001). It does not load on Classic Era, Anniversary or retail.

**Has it been tested in the live game?** Yes: it has run on the live game since launch on
Nov 4, 2026. Report anything odd as a
[GitHub issue](https://github.com/Krool/KroolWorldForever/issues) or a comment on the CurseForge page, with what
`/kw errors` prints.

**Where do Kill Value's numbers come from?** A vanilla 1.12 loot baseline (cmangos classic-db), blended
with the drop rates you record yourself as you loot. Forever may have rebalanced some loot, so creatures
you farm get more accurate over time.

**Why does Quest Trash say "keep" so often?** Every unknown fails toward keep. Tradable items are never
told "delete", and repeatable or seasonal quest items are always kept.

**Does Setups touch other characters?** Bars, macros, the addon list and per-character settings change
only on the character you apply to. Keybindings do too by default (a setting switches them to
account-wide). Some things the game stores for the whole account change for every character:
account-wide interface settings, Edit Mode's own checkboxes, and this addon's settings.

**Where do Disenchant Value's tables come from?** The vanilla 1.12 disenchant tables (cmangos
classic-db): exact for classic items, and by quality, weapon or armor and item level for items new
to Forever. Forever's disenchanting looks the same so far (same dust, essence and shard tiers);
if you see it differ, please open an issue. Auctionator has a disenchant line too, but on Forever it loads its retail
tables, so items of classic levels get none. Least Valuable and Quest Reward Value compare after the 5% auction
cut, and before any tip you give a disenchanter.

**Where do Camp Guide's numbers come from?** The camp objects' own tooltips in the 1.60.1.70790
client, level band by level band, as Endgame Tools lists them, and the camp spells in Forever's client
data (forever.warcraftdb.com). A camp buff does not stack with the class buff it copies (at level 60
the class buff gives more), so with Blessing of Might on you, the Lodestone's attack power does not
add to it.

**Why doesn't the campfire list its objects by itself?** The game gives addons no way to see the
objects around a fire. Camp Guide knows each one by the name its tooltip shows when you hover it, so
the campfire lists the ones you have hovered. It works only while you have Campfire Nearby (the aura
everyone close to a fire gets), so an inn's chair is left alone.

**Where do Skill-Up Odds' chances come from?** The game client knows each recipe's yellow and grey
skill (Skill-Up Odds reads them from Forever's own recipe data), but the chance of a point is rolled
on Blizzard's servers and has never been published. The common estimate is a straight line: 100% at
yellow, falling evenly to 0% at grey. Skill-Up Odds starts from that line and tunes it with every
yellow or green craft on all your characters: it adds up the chances the line gave your crafts and
compares that with the points you actually got. If your crafts gave 10% more points than the line
expected, every chance is 10% higher (never above 100%). The first 10 expected points are weighted
toward the plain line, so a handful of crafts cannot swing it. On the owner's account, 174 crafts
gave 67 points where the line expected 63. `/kwu` shows the comparison range by range. Orange
always gives a point and grey never does: that is the game's rule, and it is measured too. The gold
a point costs is a craft's cost (each reagent at the cheaper of its auction price and the vendor
price you have seen, minus what the result sells for) divided by the points a craft gives on
average. An auction price more than 3 days old is flagged, and it loses to any vendor price you
have seen.

**Is this allowed?** Yes. It uses only the standard addon API: tooltips, the loot window, and (for
Setups) the same bar, binding and macro calls any action bar profile addon uses, out of combat.

**Why doesn't Rare Alert just mark the rare?** Since Midnight, which Forever is built on, setting a
raid marker is protected: only a click or key press may do it. The button and key run
`/targetexact <rare>` and `/tm` for you, one press. They can change only out of combat, so a rare
found in combat gets the alert, and the button catches up when combat ends. If you already use
RareScanner or SilverDragon (both have Forever builds), turn off Rare Alert's sound and screen
message and keep the button.

## Development

```
.\scripts\link-addon.ps1 -AddOnsPath "<WoW>\_forever_\Interface\AddOns"   # junction for dev
cd tools\test; npm install; npm test                                       # all suites + API lint
.\scripts\build.ps1                                                        # dist\KroolWorldForever-<v>.zip
.\scripts\release.ps1 -Version x.y.z [-Publish]                            # see CLAUDE.md
```

- `KroolWorldForever/` is the shipped addon: `Core/` (registry, settings panel, lifecycle) and
  `Features/<Name>/` (one folder per feature).
- `tools/test/<feature>/` holds one suite per feature: a stub client plus behavior checks. Each suite
  loads the whole bundle under fengari.
- `tools/forever-api/` holds the API allowlist lint. It checks every `C_*` call, event and `Enum`
  against Forever's API docs.
- `tools/killvalue-data/` holds the Kill Value loot data generator (cmangos classic-db).
- `tools/skillup-data/`, `tools/reagents-data/` and `tools/transports-data/` regenerate the Skill-Up
  Odds, Reagent Uses and Boats And Zeppelins data from Forever's client tables. The test runner
  checks each against the API list's game build.
- `tools/standalone/` builds the KW addons from the bundle.
- `tools/bugs.js` prints the Lua errors !BugGrabber saved in your Forever install, and the ones the
  addon caught itself (`/kw errors`).
- `template/HelloForever` is a minimal addon skeleton.
